# Accepted dependency advisories for the pip-audit gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml
#
# Format: one advisory ID per line. Everything after `#` is a comment.
#
# RULES:
#   1. Every entry needs a reason and a review date. No bare IDs.
#   2. An entry is a decision to SHIP a known vulnerability. It is not a way to
#      make CI green - if you cannot write a defensible reason, fix the dependency.
#   3. Re-check every entry at its review date. Suppressions rot: a CVE with no
#      fix today usually has one in three months.
#
# To suppress nothing, leave this file with comments only - that is the goal state.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CURRENT STATUS: two entries, BOTH cleared by the same fix (the python-jose ->
# PyJWT migration). 9 of the original 10 advisories were FIXED, not
# suppressed, by upgrading fastapi 0.115.14 -> 0.136.3 and starlette
# 0.46.2 -> 1.6.0 (and earlier, python-multipart 0.0.20 -> 0.0.32).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# PYSEC-2026-1325 - ecdsa 0.19.2
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT: the Minerva attack. ecdsa is written in pure Python and cannot execute
# in constant time, so an attacker able to measure signing/verification timing
# precisely may be able to recover the private key.
#
# WHY IT IS SUPPRESSED RATHER THAN FIXED: there is no fixed version. The
# `Fix Versions` column in the pip-audit report is empty - upstream's position
# is that constant-time operation is out of scope for a pure-Python
# implementation. No version bump can clear this. Blocking every deploy on an
# advisory that cannot be actioned by upgrading does not make the system safer;
# it teaches people to bypass the gate, which does make it less safe.
#
# EXPOSURE: ecdsa arrives transitively via python-jose, which this codebase uses
# only for HS256 (see ALGORITHM in app/core/config.py). HS256 is HMAC-SHA256 -
# symmetric, no elliptic curve involved - so the vulnerable code path is not
# reached on the current configuration. This is the reason the risk is
# acceptable, and it is also the thing that would stop being true: switching
# ALGORITHM to any ES* curve algorithm makes this advisory live and immediate.
#
# THE REAL FIX: migrate python-jose -> PyJWT, which drops ecdsa from the tree
# entirely. Sized at 3 files / 5 call sites - app/core/security.py (encode),
# app/api/deps.py (decode), app/core/rate_limit.py (decode in the rate-limit
# key function),
# plus JWTError -> PyJWTError. Two gotchas: PyJWT >= 2.10 requires `sub` to be a
# string and this codebase passes a UUID, and PyJWT validates exp/nbf by
# default. It touches authentication, so it wants the full auth e2e suite behind
# it and its own PR - not a bundled drive-by.
#
# REVIEW DATE: 2026-11-27 (3 months). At review, check whether ecdsa has shipped
# a fix, and whether the python-jose -> PyJWT migration has landed. If neither,
# re-justify or do the migration - do not silently extend the date.
#
# DECIDED: 2026-08-27, Adebayo, on PR #18.
PYSEC-2026-1325
#
# CVE-2026-85394 - python-jose 3.5.0
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT: Critical (CVSS ~9.1) HS256 token forgery. python-jose accepts a
# DER-encoded public key as an HMAC secret, so a verifier that does not pin its
# algorithm can be tricked into checking an HS256 signature made with a key the
# attacker knows. An incomplete-fix follow-up to CVE-2024-33663.
#
# NOTE THE INVERSION: the ecdsa entry above is accepted *because* we only use
# HS256. This advisory makes the HS256 path itself the vulnerable one. That
# argument alone no longer covers python-jose - the exposure analysis below does.
#
# WHY IT IS SUPPRESSED RATHER THAN FIXED: there is no fixed version. 3.5.0 is
# the latest release and the pip-audit `Fix Versions` column is empty. It is
# repo-wide dependency drift, not caused by any feature PR, and it blocks every
# merge until the migration below lands.
#
# EXPOSURE: not reachable on the current configuration. The forgery needs (a) a
# verifier that does not restrict the algorithm and (b) a public key the service
# trusts. Neither exists here:
#   - both decode sites pin the algorithm: app/api/deps.py:28-29 and
#     app/core/rate_limit.py:256 pass algorithms=[settings.ALGORITHM];
#   - ALGORITHM is "HS256" (app/core/config.py:18) and the key is the symmetric
#     SECRET_KEY;
#   - there is no asymmetric public key anywhere in the app.
# What would make it live: a new decode site without `algorithms=`, or any
# RS*/ES*/PS* key material entering the verify path. Either change must land
# the migration first.
#
# THE REAL FIX: the same python-jose -> PyJWT migration described above (it
# clears this entry and PYSEC-2026-1325 together). Auth-critical: own PR, full
# auth e2e suite, security review.
#
# REVIEW DATE: 2026-11-10 (1 month - shorter than usual because the severity is
# Critical). At review, the migration should have landed and both entries be
# deleted. If not, re-justify in writing - do not silently extend the date.
#
# DECIDED: 2026-10-10, Adebayo (surfaced on PR #119).
CVE-2026-85394
